overall: The AG found the committee violated the law by failing to keep executive session minutes for 2008 and by discussing the Fire Chief's performance in executive session; it found no violation on scheduling or public speaking.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to provide executive session minutes for September 2008 meetings; the committee said those minutes never existed.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to take and retain minutes of these meetings.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged missing open session minutes, executive session minutes and tapes for 2008 and 2010-2011; most were produced after the complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We understand these to be the only requested minutes still outstanding.

allegations.summary: Complainant challenged the committee's destruction of tape recordings of the 2008 executive sessions.
allegations.key_passage: Whether it was appropriate for the Committee to destroy tape recordings of a meeting is not a matter within our jurisdiction to resolve.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee held a February 2011 meeting on his contract renewal knowing he could not attend.
allegations.key_passage: There is no requirement in the Open Meeting Law that a public body schedule a meeting so that a subject of the public body's deliberation can attend.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the public was not allowed to speak on his behalf at the February 2011 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the chair was within his power to refuse to recognize the individual during the meeting, the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: AG's own review found the committee discussed the Fire Chief's performance in executive session in 2010 when the discussions belonged in open session.
allegations.key_passage: These discussions should have occurred in open session.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
